extracted.intended_audience: research authors and peer reviewers considering submitting to or reviewing for eLife
extracted.subtask_description: Description of eLife's peer-review and publishing model (Reviewed Preprints and Version of Record), reviewer/editor responsibilities, assessment vocabulary, submission/options, fee policy, and versioning. Guidance for authors and reviewers about what is published and how reviews/assessments are presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewed Preprint publication model
rubrics_metrics.description: Publishing with eLife is different because there is no accept or reject decision after peer review: rather, every article we review is published as a Reviewed Preprint. This ... includes the article, feedback from the reviewers, a response from the author (if available), and an eLife Assessment that summarizes the significance of the findings being reported and the strength of the evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: By making the views of expert editors and reviewers an integral part of the published paper, eLife emphasizes the scientific content of individual articles rather than journal name. Reviewed Preprints can be cited by their DOI and/or their eLife citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editor selection for peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: eLife editors — who are all active researchers — discuss new submissions and decide which will be peer reviewed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The specific criteria used by the editors are discussed in a separate page (“How and why eLife selects papers for peer review”). Editors' initial evaluation determines whether a submission proceeds to the peer-review stage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Peer reviewer deliverables: Public Review and improvement recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Each peer reviewer is asked to write a Public Review of the article, and to recommend ways in which the authors could improve it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public Reviews are published as part of the Reviewed Preprint/Version of Record and should describe strengths and weaknesses and suggest concrete improvements.

rubrics_metrics.name: eLife Assessment: summarise significance and strength of evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor and the peer reviewers also write an eLife Assessment that summarises the significance of the findings and the strength of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife Assessments use a common vocabulary: significance is assessed on a scale ranging from 'landmark' to 'useful'; strength of evidence is assessed on a scale ranging from 'exceptional' to 'inadequate'. Editors and reviewers consult with each other when writing Assessments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Reviews content standards
rubrics_metrics.description: Public Reviews describe the strengths and weaknesses of the article, and indicate whether the claims and conclusions are justified by the data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the reviewers disagree with the claims in an article, this is made explicit within the eLife Assessment and the Public Reviews. Recommendations to the authors for improving the article are published as part of the Version of Record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision and versioning policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors are free to submit a revised version of their article, and the editor and the peer reviewers will update the eLife Assessment and the Public Reviews as necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Version two of the Reviewed Preprint will include the revised preprint, an updated eLife Assessment and Public Reviews (as appropriate), and a response from the authors. At any point following peer review, authors can choose to publish a Version of Record to mark the end of the review and publication process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preprint submission options and policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors may submit to eLife directly or transfer a preprint from bioRxiv or medRxiv. eLife works with authors to make all submissions selected for peer review available as preprints.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publishing in eLife combines the advantages of preprints with the scrutiny offered by peer review; Reviewed Preprints and their components (Assessment, Public Reviews, responses) are openly available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee and waiver policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Our publication fee is $3000 and is payable at the peer-review stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fee is waived for anyone who cannot afford to pay.

rubrics_metrics.name: Version of Record indexing and funder compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: Publication of an eLife Version of Record (VOR) complies with all major funding agency requirements for immediate online access to the published results of their research grants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: VORs are typically indexed by services such as Google Scholar, PubMed, PubMed Central, Europe PMC, OpenAlex, and the Directory of Open Access Journals; however, each indexing service applies different criteria and eLife cannot guarantee inclusion in all services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collaborative editorial process and limits policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Editors and reviewers consult with each other during the peer-review process, especially when writing eLife Assessments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: eLife states that it does not artificially limit the number of articles it reviews or publishes, reflecting a publication policy rather than quota-based selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Advantages and guiding values of the eLife model
rubrics_metrics.description: Advantages of the eLife approach include: (1) Less uncertainty — once an article has been selected for peer review, the authors can be sure that it will be published; (2) Speed and openness — publishing combines preprints with peer review; (3) Expert evaluations — eLife Assessments summarize significance and strength of evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These values explain the rationale for eLife's model (emphasis on openness, speed, and expert judgement) and are intended to guide authors' and reviewers' expectations about the process and outputs.
